newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian edible oil prices firm on supply shortfall.
newsitem.headline: Indian edible oil prices firm on supply shortfall.

text.p: Indian domestic edible oil prices have firmed by about 300-400 rupees a tonne in the past week due to a slowdown in arrivals, industry officials and traders said on Wednesday.
"Edible oil prices have gone up by three to four rupees per 10 kg during the last week," Navinbhai Shah, president of Bombay Oilseeds and Oil Exchange Ltd, told Reuters.
Traders said groundnut oil was currently quoted at around 35,000 rupees per tonne, palm olein at 28,300 rupees per tonne and soy oil at 28,000 rupees per tonne in domestic markets.
"Further erosion of prices has stopped because of the slowdown of arrivals in the terminal markets," Shah said.
Traders said around 200 tonnes of edible oil were currently arriving in the markets per day compared to 300 tonnes last week.
They said around 70,000 bags (one bag = 70kg) of soybeans were arriving each day in central Indian markets compared to 150,000 bags daily at the same time last year.
The central state of Madhya Pradesh accounts for nearly 80 percent of the country's soybean production.

In the western state of Gujarat, about 60,000 bags of groundnut were arriving a day compared to 50,000 bags at the same time last year. Gujarat accounts for one third of the country's groundnut output.
"Palm olein imports are also maintaining its pace. Every week, about 5,000 tonnes of imported palm olein is arriving," Shah said.
Traders said imported palm olein was currently quoted at around $610 per tonne CIF at Indian ports.
According to trade estimates, domestic oilseed production in 1996/97 (November-October) is forecast at 21.5 million tonnes, of which winter output will account for 11.9 million tonnes.
Domestic oilseed output in 1995/96 was around 21 million tonnes.
India harvests two oilseed crops, getting the bulk of the output from the winter crop. Sowing for the winter crop is done in July and the harvest starts in October.
